obligations.source_text: culture agents start (and --all) skips backend: external agents and prints who owns their lifecycle, before any fork: today _run_multi_agents forks a child per agent that dies in _resolve_daemon_factory (cli/agents.py:797-819) with 'unknown agent backend' after the parent already printed 'Started'

obligations.behavior: For a backend: external agent: sends no signal, sends no IPC, touches no pidfile, prints 'owned by <owner>', exits 0
obligations.source_text: culture agents stop skips backend: external agents with the same owner message: stop_agent (cli/shared/process.py:21) only knows the agent IPC socket and the agent-<nick> pidfile, neither of which an external process has

obligations.seam: culture agents status (cli/shared/display.py) <-> agentirc PRESENCE LIST
obligations.behavior: An external agent's row shows its PRESENCE state when the server answers, and 'unknown' when it is unreachable. Harness agent rows are byte-identical to before
obligations.source_text: culture agents status shows an external agent's state from the live PRESENCE registry (PRESENCE LIST, as resource_view._query_presence_wire already does), not from agent_process_status (cli/shared/display.py:18-31), which reads only the pidfile + IPC socket and would always print 'stopped'

obligations.behavior: Every resident row carries a backend field: the manifest backend for registered nicks, null for unregistered ones. The envelope {supported, generated_at, residents} is unchanged
obligations.source_text: /residents.json needs no culture change to list an external resident: fetch_residents_async (resource_view.py:329-349) lists every nick in agentirc's PRESENCE registry and apply_budgets only joins the manifest for budget fields, so a manifest-less or external nick is still listed

obligations.behavior: For an external agent: install writes no systemd unit, and each IPC verb exits non-zero with the owner message rather than a socket error
obligations.source_text: Every other per-agent verb that assumes a culture-owned daemon refuses an external agent with the owner message instead of failing obscurely: install (would write a crashing culture-agent-<nick> systemd unit via persistence.install_service, cli/agents.py:1439), and the IPC verbs sleep/wake/learn/message/read (_resolve_ipc_targets, cli/agents.py:1126)

obligations.behavior: NICK of an account's nick without successful SASL PLAIN, or with a wrong or revoked secret, never gets 001 RPL_WELCOME. With the right secret it gets 001. This holds whether or not the real agent is connected
obligations.source_text: agentirc keeps agent accounts (nick, secret hash, role, channel grants, revoked flag) and refuses registration of an account's nick until SASL PLAIN authenticates against it. Today _handle_nick checks only the system- prefix, the <server>- prefix and live collision (client.py:461-486), and the only ownership checks are room-owner checks (skills/rooms.py:334,478). culture is the admin surface that writes accounts from the manifest. agentirc and cultureagent (shared irc_transport.py:135-136 sends SASL) are sibling hand-offs

obligations.behavior: The generated unit contains LoadCredential=<nick-secret>:<operator store path>. The agent reads its secret only from $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY. No plaintext secret appears in the working dir, env, argv, ~/.culture agent files or logs
obligations.source_text: culture agents register creates the agent's mesh account and mints its secret (plaintext shown once, SHA-256 stored, as irc-lens agent_credentials does). Units culture generates (persistence.install_service, the [Service] block at persistence.py:295) get a LoadCredential= line for that secret, and culture agents start reads it from CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY and hands it to the shared transport. An external owner adds the same LoadCredential= line to its own unit

obligations.behavior: A nick with no account registers exactly as on agentirc today (prefix + collision checks only). Upgrading server and culture without re-registering changes no existing agent's connect, join or speak behaviour
obligations.source_text: No flag day: agentirc enforces a nick only once the server holds a credential for it. Agents registered before this change keep connecting until they are re-registered or have a credential minted. culture doctor lists registered agents that have no credential

obligations.behavior: No account, secret hash, grant or role field is carried in any S2S message
obligations.source_text: Reservation is enforced only on the nick's home server. Every nick carries its <server>- prefix and agentirc already refuses a non-matching prefix (client.py:470-476), so credential tables are never federated across linked servers

obligations.behavior: JOIN to a channel with no grant is refused with a numeric error. A read-only grant joins but its PRIVMSG to the channel is refused. Grants are seeded from culture.yaml channels:. DMs aren't gated
obligations.source_text: Channel grants are enforced by agentirc: an authenticated agent account may JOIN and speak only in channels its grants allow, with grant levels mirroring irc-lens grants(email, resource_kind, resource, level). Grants are seeded from the agent's culture.yaml channels: list (config.py:94, default ['#general']), so existing agents keep their channels

obligations.seam: agentirc role check on admin / room-owner verbs
obligations.behavior: A resident or guest account sending an operator-only verb is refused. An operator account succeeds. A guest can't be granted a channel outside its sandbox
obligations.source_text: Roles live on the account and gate what it may do. culture sets the role at register time, and agentirc enforces it

obligations.seam: culture agents revoke/rotate CLI + agentirc session + audit log
obligations.behavior: Revoke closes the live session within 5 s and refuses every reconnect. Rotate makes the old secret fail and the restarted unit connect. The audit log gains exactly one line per account change, containing no secret material
obligations.source_text: Operators can revoke and rotate an agent's secret from the culture CLI. Revoking disconnects the live session and blocks reconnects. Rotating issues a new secret, updates the unit's credential and restarts the unit (or tells the external owner). Every account change (create, rotate, revoke, grant, role) is appended to an audit log keyed by account, never containing a secret

obligations.behavior: After 001, Gwen sets user mode +A and publishes PRESENCE with a valid state. Her row turns offline on QUIT or a dropped TCP connection
obligations.source_text: The external process carries the presence contract itself: agentirc creates a row only on a PRESENCE :<json> publish (agentirc skills/presence.py:250) and flips it offline only on QUIT or a TCP close from a +A/+C client (skills/presence.py:108-120) - so Gwen's daemon must set user mode +A and publish PRESENCE (idle at minimum) to appear and to go offline correctly

obligations.seam: culture-generated systemd unit + grant store (grant.store, grant run --inject)
obligations.behavior: The generated ExecStart is wrapped in grant run --inject CULTURE_AGENT_SECRET=<hidden secret name> --. The secret exists only in the grant store and, briefly, in the daemon process environment before it is removed. No plaintext appears in the working dir, ~/.culture, argv, logs or any child process environment
obligations.source_text: culture agents register creates the agent's mesh account, mints its secret with grant.generate.random_secret, stores it as a hidden grant secret named after the nick (e.g. CULTURE_AGENT_SPARK_GWEN), and writes only its SHA-256 hash into the account. Units culture generates (persistence.install_service, persistence.py:295) wrap ExecStart in grant run --inject CULTURE_AGENT_SECRET=<name> --. An external owner (Gwen's unit, the sbx/ask units) wraps its own ExecStart the same way

obligations.behavior: Every grant verb is reachable as culture secret <verb> with identical argv, exit code, stdout and stderr. Hidden-secret refusals and admin mode behave as in grant itself
obligations.source_text: culture moves from shushu to grant. grant becomes a capped dependency (grant>=0.11,<0.12). culture secret, today an unimplemented 'coming soon' namespace in culture_core/cli/introspect.py _NAMESPACES, becomes a forward to grant through the culture_core/cli/_passthrough.py pattern (culture secret <verb> == grant <verb>). The docs that name shushu now name grant: README.md:38,63, docs/culture/vision.md:70, docs/reference/cli/devex.md:71

obligations.behavior: On 904/905/908, a refused nick while holding a secret, a server without SASL PLAIN or a sasl NAK, the transport stops reconnecting and the runner exits 78
obligations.source_text: On a SASL failure (904/905 or a refused nick) the shared transport stops reconnecting and the daemon exits with the permanent-failure status, so systemd stops restarting it. Today _reconnect (cultureagent clients/shared/irc_transport.py:271-283) retries forever with backoff capped at 60 s, so a revoked agent would hammer the server indefinitely

obligations.behavior: After CAP LS, no 001 and no SNICK until CAP END; a client that never sends CAP registers as before
obligations.source_text: agentirc must hold registration while CAP negotiation is open. Today _try_register (agentirc client.py:512-519) completes on NICK+USER, sends 001 and announces SNICK to linked peers immediately, so SASL can't gate anything until registration waits for CAP END. No SNICK for an account nick may go out before authentication succeeds

obligations.behavior: Every failed auth logs nick, peer and reason without secret material; failures are rate-limited per (address, account); culture.auth.failures counts them by reason
obligations.source_text: agentirc logs every failed authentication (nick, peer address, reason, never the secret) and rate-limits failed attempts per peer address. The counts are exposed as culture.* telemetry so a brute force or a misconfigured agent is visible

obligations.behavior: CULTURE_AGENT_SECRET is read once and removed from os.environ before connecting or spawning; child processes never see it
obligations.source_text: The daemon reads CULTURE_AGENT_SECRET once at startup and removes it from os.environ before connecting or spawning anything, so agent tool subprocesses (shell tools, SDK children) never inherit it. grant run --inject delivers it through the environment, and children inherit the environment by default
